MIND. [1] [Lyss.]
Memory for single words much improved.
Strange notions and apprehensions during pregnancy.
Mania spermatica ; stallions.
Inclination to be rude and abusive, to bite and strike. θ Diarrhœa.
Break out of their stables furiously and run or jump over ditches and fences. θ Lyssa of sheep.
No afraid of dogs, but dislikes to see them because their sight renews her fear. θ Lyssophobia.
Exhilarated, felt as if he had received joyful intelligence.
Lyssophobia ; fear of becoming mad.
Feels he cannot physically endure his fears much longer, and shall be compelled to go into an insane asylum. θ Lyssophobia.
Mary M., æt. 17, had been bitten several years previously by a dog, and reading of several cases of hydrophobia as reported in papers, was found in following condition : crouched in corner of a sofa, dark red bloated face, expression of terror in face, eyes glistening, conjunctiva injected red ; was brought into this condition by endeavoring to take a drink of water, and could not hear water mentioned without a shudder of fear, could not swallow, pulse very high, tongue dry and coated red ; Lyssin 2c one dose ; she was better next day, but had several slight attacks afterwards, always induced by running of water, but always yielding to remedy ; has not had an attack in nearly a year.
A musician received a bite from a small pet dog in calf of left leg while walking through a dark entry ; the bite was very slight, scarcely wounding skin ; the animal was in a healthy condition and remained so ; a pain in bitten place kept returning from time to time independently of mind dwelling on it, until finally it grew to a burning which extended through entire body, causing an indescribably strange sensation ; in night trembling, and a tormenting fear that he would have hydrophobia ; was thirsty and drank water freely ; it was two years after the bite when these and the following symptoms appeared : frequent spitting of saliva all through day, only ceasing awhile after taking strong tea in evening ; disturbed dreams at night ; finally could not partake of food or drink, and complained of pricking stitches under tongue ; mental excitement now as all his life, affects him badly ; hot vapor relieved burning pain in bite, and Lyssin 2c (Jenichen) improved all symptoms rapidly ; in three weeks he considered himself cured, and started on a journey.
Ill humor. θ Headache. θ Diarrhœa.
Felt same rheumatic pain his brother complained of. θ Lyssophobia.
Restless, constant bleating in a hoarse voice. θ Lyssa of sheep.
Sometimes he could control inclination to stool by a strong effort of will, but effort caused much nervous irritation. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Attacks of nervous headache become awful and insupportable if he hears water run out of a hydrant.
When he hears water poured out, or if he hears it run, or if he sees it, he becomes very irritable, nervous ; it causes desire for stool and other ailments.
Mental emotion always makes him worse.
Frequent gaping without being sleepy, most when he has to listen to others.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Lyss.]
Peculiar lightness in head ; lightness after nausea.
Dizziness : as if something was drawing around in a circle, and as if she could not hold her head straight ; after lying down, like a shock in upper part of brain ; with inclination to fall to right when stooping ; towards evening in upper part of head, as if she would fall, while walking ; frequent and transient ; with dim sight while walking and sitting ; and nausea ; with cramps in abdomen ; temporarily > by return of diarrhœa ; < by teaching, spelling, or being obliged to notice letters ; after lying down in bed, shock in upper part of brain ; dimness of vision on rising from stooping ; on rising from a chair, staggers ; while sitting ; on rising, cannot walk straight.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Lyss.]
Rush of blood to head : while lying down ; from chest upward, with toothache ; during pregnancy ; when rising.
Maddening outward pressing pain in forehead ; he presses his head against the wall.
Beating, throbbing headache : most severe in right temple and above right eye ; each bone feels shattered and sore ; from temple to temple.
Violent headache, most in temples and forehead, < during day and from stooping and stirring about. θ Uterine disease.
Frequent pressure on vertex, as if a cast, which fitted top of head, was pressing it down.
Pain as if head would burst. θ Pregnancy.
Afternoon, pain in head ; sick headache.
Headaches from bite of dogs, rabid or not.
At noon slight headache, lasting all day.
Burning aching from left side of occiput down neck.
Violent headache and backache.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Lyss.]
Sight of water : agitation ; renews idea of pain ; causes convulsions (pregnancy).
Since five years could not read longer than a few minutes at a time, when she would see letters double and would read something else than the right words ; had tried all sorts of spectacles without benefit, was often ashamed because she could not sign her name properly.
Could not see or hear. θ Lyssa.
Sore eyes and some fever after a bite in nose.
Inflamed, dim, watery, staring eyes, with very much dilated pupils, upper lid drawn up, and diminished sight. θ Lyssa.
Great inflammation in an eye from which gushes foamy pus ; pustules around eye ; in morning lid puffed up like an eggshell, small pustules on one finger. θ Dogbite.
Swelling of eyelids after bite of dogs. θ In sheep.
Extreme ulceration of eye, lids closed and puffed up by pus. θ In sheep.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Lyss.]
Hearing water poured out in next room makes him very irritable and nervous.
During his attacks of chronic headache, which come after mental emotion or excessive mental exertion and last a day or two, he cannot bear to hear running water ; if hydrant is allowed to run in an adjoining room, or even if water is poured into a basin, his headache increases to an insupportable degree.
After the pain following an evacuation had lessened, and he was sitting at open window, the large street waterplug was opened to cleanse the streets, and as soon as he noticed water running down gutter in front of his house, he was seized with violent pains and had to go at once to the watercloset. θ Dysentery.
If during night, or in morning before rising, he heard pouring out of water in next room, he was immediately obliged to rise and have an evacuation. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Hearing water poured out brought on convulsions. θ Pregnancy.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Lyss.]
Appearance peculiar ; skin sallow, pale or anemic ; bloated all over, but no "pitting". θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Pain in left cheek near nose, from fifth to seventh day ; followed by a hard, painless swelling of size of a pea, turned redder on thirtieth day, and became covered with a small scab ; on thirty-second day it grew soft and turned bluish red, particularly around edges ; on puncturing, a disagreeable yet not severe pain at some distance from swelling and more inside of cheek ; a small quantity of blood and matter was discharged ; on fortieth day the place ceased to discharge and healed.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Lyss.]
Masseter muscles not affected by spasms.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Lyss.]
Grinding of teeth.
Toothache and other complaints during pregnancy, with internal ebullition of blood from chest to head ; head feels as if filled with air to bursting.
Aching in swollen gums on right side.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Lyss.]
Difficult, incorrect speech. θ Stricture of throat.
Impediment in his speech, would begin a sentence with difficulty after several fruitless attempts ; some palatal vowels he could not pronounce, others but incorrectly. θ Spasms of throat.
Tongue large, pale and flabby. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Pricking sensation under tongue. θ Lyssophobia.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Lyss.]
Constant sensation of intense dryness of mouth and throat. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Tough, short frothy phlegm in mouth (horse).
Large quantities of tough saliva in mouth, with constant spitting. θ Diarrhœa.
Spits all the time small quantities of a frothy saliva ; with pain in limbs.
Frequent spitting. θ Lyssophobia.
At 10 A. M. began to spit a great deal, continuing all day till supper. θ Lyssophobia.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Lyss.]
Slight redness of palate and throat, with spasm of œsophagus and difficult speech.
Sore throat, as after swallowing red pepper.
Sore throat, constant desire to swallow ; much saliva and feeling as if beaten.
Periodical spasm of œsophagus, continual painful inclination to swallow without being able to swallow anything ; constriction is most severe when taking water into mouth, if he tried to swallow it forcibly, he had burning and stinging pain in throat, cough and retching which forced fluid from his mouth ; difficult speech.
Difficulty in swallowing ; particularly fluids.
Constant desire to swallow, painful and ineffectual. θ Spasm of throat. θ Stricture of throat.
When taking water into mouth, constriction was greatest. θ Spasm of throat.
Periodical spasm of œsophagus. θ Stricture of throat.
Had difficulty in speaking ; a connected sentence could only be uttered after making several fruitless attempts ; palatic letters could not be pronounced at all, or were pronounced wrong. θ Œsophageal spasms.
Burning stinging in throat. θ Stricture of œsophagus.
Trying to swallow water forcibly, it caused burning and stinging in throat, besides cough and gagging, which forced out contents of mouth. θ Spasm of throat.
A slight redness of affected parts. θ Spasm of throat.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Lyss.]
Appetite good, but digestion deficient ; a portion of nearly everything he ate passing bowels in an undigested state. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Want of appetite. θ Hydrophobia of sheep.
Could take no nourishment (with spitting), could not remain at table. θ Lyssophobia.
Felt very thirsty and had no aversion to drink, on contrary drank large quantities of water. θ Lyssophobia.
Had not been drinking any water for some time, only some hot tea. θ Dysentery.
Drank some strong tea at supper, after which salivation discontinued until 8 P. M., then commenced again. θ Lyssophobia.
Excessive desire for salt.
Abnormal cravings during pregnancy.
Aversion to water of place he arrived at. --s. b.
Aversion to drinking water, but can take small quantities of chocolate. θ Diarrhœa.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Lyss.]
Gagging when he forcibly attempts to swallow water, forces it out of his mouth. θ Spasm of throat.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Lyss.]
Painful throbbing as if an abscess was forming in region of spleen, but very deep in, exact locality is half way between median line and outline of left side ; it lasted eight days ; with it departed remnant of a similar affection in this locality, against which eleven years of allopathic treatment had proved of no avail.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Lyss.]
General soreness in whole of lower abdomen.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Lyss.]
Tenesmus during and after stool.
Dysenteric stools with tenesmus ; renewed as soon as he hears or sees water run.
When in morning some water was poured out from pitcher into basin, pain and desire to stool returned. θ Dysentery.
When he sees or hears running water, violent pain and tenesmus return ; in a case of dysentery in Summer, of six weeks' standing, in which stools were most frequent in night, consisted of bloody mucus and were followed by pains in rectum and small of back, which forced patient to walk about in spite of great weakness ; could neither stand nor lie down ; had drank no water whole time, only hot tea occasionally.
Stools watery and profuse, with severe pains in lower bowels ; frequency of stools not uniform, some days five or six, others fifteen or twenty, usually more frequent in morning. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Chronic diarrhœa contracted in Southern camps.
Stools of bloody mucus. θ Diarrhœa.
Straining to evacuate, causing a violent pain in small of back and in rectum, afterwards compelling him to walk about, although weak. θ Dysentery.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Lyss.]
Urine too scanty and high colored. θ Chronic camp diarrhœa.
Constant desire to urinate on seeing running water ; urinates a little at a time.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Lyss.]
Strong erections, without sexual excitement or thoughts, in evening while undressing in a cold room.
Increased sexual desire. θ Dropsy of spine with sheep. θ Hydrophobia of sheep.
Satyriasis in a stallion ; hot breath streamed from nostrils.
Semen is discharged too late or not at all during coition.
Hydrocele.
Atrophy of testicles ; testicles diminish in size, first left, then right.
Complaints resulting from abnormal sexual desire.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Lyss.]
Aphrodisiac sense deficient. θ Prolapsus uteri.
Insatiable heat ; with cows.
With a painful sensitiveness of womb, slight degree of prolapsus, so that after any considerable physical effort there would be a strong conviction that it was prolapsed.
Considerable pain in lower part of back, with a soreness felt through pubic region, which was clearly proved to be in neck of womb by an increase of pain from pressing finger on neck ; principally at point where finger came in contact with womb. θ Subjective prolapsus.
Womb high up in abdomen, enlarged in top and fundus.
Abrasion about os tincæ (treated with caustic), some tumefaction of cervix and walls of vagina remained, showing a low degree of inflammation. θ Prolapsus.
Speculum showed os tincæ of size of a small goose quill, smooth and normal, except that there was a string of bloody mucus of size of os hanging from it, so tough and viscid that it was difficult to wipe it away with a sponge. θ Subjective prolapsus.
Swelling of womb in all its parts, extending somewhat into vagina. θ Prolapsus.
Bright redness of vaginal portion of womb. θ Prolapsus.
After menses found that prolapsed uterus, a case considered incurable, was in its proper position, and continued so after an interval of two months, though she has done much to test the cure, lifting a heavy child in and out of bed at night, when she was necessarily without her supporter.
Prolapsus uteri of seven years' standing.
Metritis, prolapsus or induration of uterus ; in cows.
Menstruation, with hemorrhoids, pulsations in anus and weakness of back.
Menses rather frequent, protracted, dark, and at times fetid. θ Prolapsus uteri.
During interval of menses "a show" that seemed quite obstinate. θ Prolapsus uteri.
Anemia in consequence of disturbed sexual function.
Severe leucorrhœa, with pains in back and lower part of bowels ; sore vagina.
Sensitiveness of vagina rendering coition quite painful. θ Prolapsus uteri.
Menses too profuse, at times a little too frequent. θ Prolapsus.
Weakness in back, with copious catamenia.
Tearing, followed by pressing downward, could not make a hard step during catamenia.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Lyss.]
During pregnancy ; strange notions, desires or cravings ; rush of blood from chest upward ; toothache, backache and other complaints ; great sense of bearing down ; intense pain from inflammation of os and cervix (formerly treated with Caustic.) ; great soreness in lower part of back and bowels.
All changes of position that tilt or rotate to a moderate extent the os uteri cause much pain. θ During pregnancy.
Spasms excited whenever she attempts to drink water, or if she hears it poured from one vessel into another ; sight or sound of water affects unpleasantly, even though desiring water. θ Puerperal convulsions.
Since childbirth more pain with coition and a dislike to it. θ Subjective prolapsus.
Since cessation of lochia a severe leucorrhœa ; pain in back and lower part of bowels ; soreness of vagina.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Lyss.]
Pain next to larynx, on right side, felt on turning neck and on pressure.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Lyss.]
Hot breath streams from nostrils. θ Satyriasis in a stallion.
Sighing, with pain in heart.
Dyspnœa : with flatulency, cough and rattling in chest ; with sighing, groaning respiration ; from cardiac pain ; < lying down.
   

COUGH. [27] [Lyss.]
Coughing when attempting to swallow water forcibly, forces it out of mouth. θ Spasm of throat.
Cough and gagging. θ Stricture of throat.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Lyss.]
Gangrene of lungs, caused by pneumonia and sexual excitement. θ Satyriasis in a stallion.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Lyss.]
Stitches in heart, more while walking ; they would kill him if they continued.
Heart had for three months not been free from a sticking, drawing, squeezing pain, result of an attack of rheumatism and cold, together with a palpitation and difficulty of breathing.
Pain in cardiac region, to which he is subject, is < half an hour after, but much > in several days.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Lyss.]
Backache and headache.
Sheep turn and wriggle their backs because they cannot bear heat of sun ; increased sexual excitement ; symptoms pointing to madness ; scratching their backs appears to be agreeable to them, as they remain quiet and make a peculiar motion with their mouths, which does not express pain.
Great weakness in back, as if it would split and fall apart. θ Lyssophobia.
A sore lameness in back, with some degree of soreness in lower abdomen. θ Prolapsus uteri.
Considerable pain in lower part of back, with a soreness felt through to pubic region ; pressing finger on neck increased it.
Disease peculiar to sheep, termed the "gid ;" dropsy of spine.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Lyss.]
A pressive pain in right hip bone, goes from there to middle of sacral bone.
Ulcers on legs, with emaciation and coldness, left side ; contraction of hamstrings and relaxation of ligaments of ankle joint and flexors of toes.
The pain in calf came even when he was not thinking of bite at all ; lately much < and quite severe. θ Lyssophobia.
Great swelling in heel of a cow from dog-bite ; very restless.
   

NERVES. [36] [Lyss.]
He could neither lie down nor stand up for any length of time. θ Dysentery.
Continual trembling sensation through whole body. θ Lyssophobia.
The strange feeling changed during night into a trembling, and he is full of fear. θ Lyssophobia.
Attacks returned every few minutes, for five hours, until they were arrested ; pain passing down spine to loins and hips, and from thence to knees.
Convulsions daily ; rolls head from side to side ; winking and rolling eyes ; attempts to bite others ; pelvis and legs are turned to one side as far as possible. θ Child, æt. 2, after scarlatina.
At times a singular sensation, a kind of "die away" feeling, quite instantaneous, cannot describe it ; seems to extend through heart to back, accompanied with quivering around breast bones and pain in nerves, from left side of chest to throat and left jaw ; fluttering about heart.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Lyss.]
Frequent yawning, without sleepiness, particularly when hearing others yawn.
Passed most of his nights sleeplessly, walking up and down in despair. θ Lyssophobia.
During night slept but little ; was disturbed by disagreeable, disconnected dreams ; felt strangely. θ Lyssophobia.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Lyss.]
Burning sensation in bitten place > by hot steam striking against it. θ Lyssophobia.
Unbearableness of heat of sun. θ Dropsy of spine with sheep.
   

FEVER. [40] [Lyss.]
Intermittent fever.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Lyss.]
First day >, next day < ; on third day salivation returned. θ Lyssophobia.
Periodically since two weeks. θ Spasm of throat.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Lyss.]
Drawing from neck to forehead, immediately followed by sparks before eyes and vanishing of sight ; red face ; involuntary grinding of teeth ; second attack ; the first was felt in head after washing in morning ; seven days after bite of mad dog (Bellad. [300], three doses, Hyosc. interpolated once a day).
   

TISSUES. [44] [Lyss.]
Chlorosis.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Lyss.]
A bite of an angry dog into right thigh had not healed, turned into malignant ulcers ; surrounding bluish red edges, raised and hard, bases badly suppurating and ichorous, with redness and hardness.
Scars from a bite in nose swollen and red for fifteen months.
Ulcers remaining after bite of evil disposed dogs.
Pain on spot bitten became burning, and extended over whole body, and he felt very strangely. θ Lyssophobia.
Felt a continued pain in spot on right calf where he was bitten, but without a lesion. θ Lyssophobia.
Wounds from bite of dogs, in sheep.
A cow bitten by a dog in foot joint had a large swelling of part, and animal got very restless. --s. b.
Two puppies, bitten by their rabid mother, did not get mad after taking Lyssin.
   

SKIN. [46] [Lyss.]
Bluish discoloration of bitten place (after Laches.).
Pustules : on forehead ; around inflamed eye ; on finger (after bite).
Malignant ulcers from bite of a dog.
Red scar from bite of a dog.
Cancerous sores.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Lyss.]
Antidotes : Bellad., Hyosc., Stramon.
